findings.text: Within one paragraph a newcomer learns what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves. The page answers 'what is it' and 'why does it matter' straight away.
findings.source: header, first lede paragraph: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The first section after the header is a raw failure message. It sits where the lede promises proof of models, cost and verdict. A newcomer gets no evidence for that promise, and the leaked error makes the page look broken.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The page pitches Athena, but almost all of it is a detailed study of a different tool, firstmate. A newcomer may be unsure which project the page is about until the third lede paragraph explains what a study is.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> and "This page is that study of firstmate."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete and in order: prerequisites, clone, install, then a first command. A link near the top jumps here, so the 'what to do next' question is well served.
findings.source: Next steps: "Get the code: git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "Install Athena from the checkout: ./setup.sh" ... "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: This link is aimed at the project owner, not a visitor, and nothing on the page says what the proposals are. A newcomer may follow it and get confused.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The section promises three parts but contains four subheadings, starting with "Words used first". Its opening sentence about firstmate is then repeated almost word for word in the first bullet of "What firstmate is".
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term has no definition in the source. That is honest, but it leaves a newcomer without working meanings for words the transition cards rely on.
findings.source: Glossary entries for captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat and wake: "The firstmate source does not define ..."

findings.text: The state, transition and claim detail is thorough and every claim links to its source lines. For a first visit it is dense, though, and most newcomers will skim past it. It shows Athena's traceability better than it explains firstmate to someone new.
findings.source: Transitions, Counters, Claims and sources sections

findings.text: This refers to the internal layout of the repository and means nothing to a visitor who has not cloned it.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
